messages.author: a5ca085497920157
messages.subject: Announcement: Rhipe 0.67
parts:
Greetings,

I am happy to announce that we have pushed out a new version of Rhipe
(0.67). Various aspects of this version were contributed by Saptarshi
Guha, Jeremah Rounds (myself), and Ryan Hafen. Saptarshi Guha asked
me to make the announcement.

It is available for download from here: https://github.com/saptarshiguha/RHIPE/downloads

We are assembling version changes here:
https://github.com/saptarshiguha/RHIPE/wiki/Version-History-and-Notes


The major goal of this version was something that the average user
would not notice which is that "R CMD check Rhipe_0.67.tar.gz" reports
no warnings or notes about the package; previously it would get quite
upset. However in addition to meeting that goal, some quality of life
changes and bug fixes went into the new version.

= New rhoptions() =

rhoptions(zip= ...) and rhoptions(mapred=...) are now usable to set
defaults for all subsequent rhmr calls. This is helpful in separating
out your cluster/location specific parameters from your job/task
specific parameters.

= New Job Monitoring =

The new function rhwatch() is now being engineered as the monitoring
function, so all these should work:
rhwatch(mr)
rhwatch(rhex(mr))
rhwatch("some_job_id")

= New HDFS Working Directories =

To help along portability, we also have hdfs.setwd() and hdfs.getwd()
which set paths to use as the base of subsequent relative paths. For
example consider:
hdfs.setwd("/wsc/jrounds")
mr = rhmr(..., ifolder="data09.in", ofolder="data09.out")

This now means take the ifolder as /wsc/jrounds/data09.in and take
the ofolder as /wsc/jrounds/data09.out, but this call continues to
have the same meaning it always had and does not use the HDFS working
directory.
mr = rhmr(..., ifolder="/data09.in", ofolder="/data09.out")

Those of you that test jobs on laptops or small clusters and then do
work on production clusters can use the new site specific rhoptions()
and hdfs.setwd to make your code easier to move around.

= Additionally =

Those people that build runners and Rhipe MapReduce archives will
want to note that imperious.so has been renamed "RhipeMapReduce" to be
clearer to new users. There is now an easy way to find the location
of this executable use: rhoptions()$RhipeMapReduce. You should only
need to rewrite your scripts to make use of the new RhipeMapReduce
where previously they used imperious.so to use the new executable.

I have an experimental function called "bashRhipeArchive". If the
user is using a bash shell it outputs a copy of a usable archive to
the current R working directory and places a copy of that archive on
the HDFS at the current HDFS working directory. If it works right
there is nothing else the user needs to do, and it reports the new
rhoptions() to make use of the archive for running MapReduce jobs, but
it is experimental.

Also, there are number changes that Saptarshi worked on such as
default tmp directories for certain calls. In addition to streaming
lining a couple of use cases such as rhmr now defaults to
inout=c("lapply","sequence") when N is not NA.



= Thanks =

Thanks for using Rhipe. Let us know if there is anything we can help
you with.

Jeremiah

messages.author: 5b0c9158bfa781ba
messages.subject: Re: [rhipe] Announcement: Rhipe 0.67
parts:
With regards to this: when ofolder is missing in rhmr, the rhmr function creates a folder in the 
HDFS folder rhabsolute.hdfs.path(rhoptions()$HADOOP.TMP.FOLDER) (which needs to be set manually, else it is NA)
the file created can be found in rhmr(..)[[1]]$rhipe_output_folder.  Example


rhwatch(z<- rhmr(map=map,reduce=NA, inout=c(NA,'seq'),jarfiles="/user/sguha/tmp/rhipecrashreport.jar",mapred=mapred),read=FALSE)

1. reduce=NA implies mapred.reduce.tasks=0
2. rhwatch will start and monitor the job, and will not read the results back in (read=FALSE, by default read=TRUE)
3. the output is stored in z[[1]]$rhipe_output_folder (e.g. 

> z[[1]]$rhipe_output_folder
[1] "/user/sguha/tmp/rhipe-temp-de755b0879eb590498345b53532caa86/"

)
4. From ?rhwatch
If the state is SUCCEEDED and total output size (in MB) is less
     than ‘rhoptions()$max.read.in.size’ the data is read with a
     warning if the number of records is more than
     ‘rhoptions()$reduce.output.records.warn’. If
     ‘rhoptions()$rhmr.max.records.to.read.in’ is not NA, that many
     records is read. This only works for Sequence output.

5. others, incase the user is not aware
rhoptions()$templates$scalarsummer is a summer reducer (e.g. wordcount) and be given to reduce in rhmr
rhoptions()$templates$colsummer is a column summer (in rhcollect, pass a matrix as the value, it's columns will be summed)


To echo Jeremiah, thanks for using RHIPE. If you have requests or issues, post here or submit to github.

Cheers
Saptarshi
